- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is bearish, model often underestimates downside; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +1.00 to -1.00), model fails to adjust quickly; apply lag correction: delay forecast shift by 1–2 days.  
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model overestimates volatility; cap forecast range within ±3% of recent 7-day moving average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes followed by recovery, model tends to underestimate rebound; add 1–2% upward bias in 3–5 day horizon.
